replacements.new:
VA deadlines after you leave the military

These dates come from VA.gov and can change, so check the linked VA page before you act. Still serving? Keep your SGLI. The dates below count from the day you leave the military.

WhenWhat VA saysSource
First 120 days after you leaveSGLI coverage continues for 120 days after you leave the military (up to 2 years if you apply and qualify for the SGLI Disability Extension). In this window you can also convert SGLI to a permanent individual policy without proof of good health.VA.gov: SGLI
Updated Nov 19, 2026; checked November 2026
Within 240 days of leavingApply for VGLI and you do not need to prove you are in good health.VA.gov: VGLI
Updated Oct 13, 2026; checked November 2026
240 days to 1 year and 120 daysYou can still apply for VGLI, but you need to send evidence that you are in good health. VA's deadline to apply is 1 year and 120 days after you leave.VA.gov: VGLI
Updated Oct 13, 2026; checked November 2026
Nov 1, 2026 to Jan 31, 2027VGLI premium holiday: if you are an eligible veteran covered by VGLI, VA says you do not need to pay VGLI premiums from November 1, 2026, through January 31, 2027, and your coverage continues. VA’s VGLI page explains who is eligible.VA.gov: VGLI
Updated Oct 13, 2026; checked November 2026
Within 120 days of separation, divorce or the member's deathA spouse can convert FSGLI spouse coverage to a permanent individual policy, such as whole life. Coverage for a child cannot be converted.VA.gov: FSGLI
Updated Oct 14, 2026; checked November 2026
Any time after a service-connected rating (age 80 or younger)VALife is open to veterans 80 or younger with a service-connected rating, even 0%. There is no time limit to apply after the rating. Full coverage starts 2 years after you apply.VA.gov: VALife
Updated Oct 13, 2026; checked November 2026
If you have S-DVIS-DVI stopped taking new applications after December 31, 2022. If you have it, you can keep it. If you apply for VALife on or after January 1, 2026, your S-DVI ends the day VA approves VALife, and you will not have full coverage during VALife's 2-year wait. S-DVI premium waivers do not carry over to VALife.VA.gov: S-DVI
Updated Nov 19, 2026; checked November 2026
If VA gave you a Specially Adapted Housing grantVMLI is mortgage life insurance of up to $200,000, paid to your lender, for veterans with a severe service-connected disability who hold title to the home, have a mortgage on it and are under 70.VA.gov: VMLI
Updated Jun 4, 2025; checked November 2026

Disclaimer: Honorbrook Insurance is an independent insurance agency. replacements.new:
Disclaimer: Honorbrook Insurance is an independent insurance agency. This page is for general educational purposes only and is not insurance, tax, or legal advice, an offer of coverage, or a contract. Product availability, benefits, riders, conversion privileges, and eligibility vary by state, carrier, and individual circumstances.

SGLI, VGLI, FSGLI, VALife, S-DVI and VMLI are VA life insurance programs. Their rules, deadlines and rates can change, so check VA.gov before you decide. Each carrier decides whether to issue a private policy. Under current federal tax law, life insurance proceeds a beneficiary receives are generally not counted as taxable income; interest on the proceeds is taxable. Individual circumstances vary, so consult a qualified tax professional.

Honorbrook Insurance is not connected with or endorsed by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, the Department of Defense, any branch of the armed forces, or any government agency or program. We do not sell VA insurance. Private premiums depend on age, sex, health, tobacco status, state, coverage amount, and carrier underwriting.
